# Adjudication Task — Chapter 579

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃579화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|서걱!
  6|
  7|한 줄기 섬광이 가슴을 가로지른 순간, 송천우는 눈앞이 아득해지는 것을 느꼈다.
  8|
  9|‘뜨겁다.’
 10|
 11|그건 벼락이었다.
 12|
 13|혼란하고 위태롭던 대격변의 한 줄을 장식했던 옛 영웅조차 막을 수 없었던 벼락.
 14|
 15|송천우는 떨리는 눈빛으로 손에 들린 검을 바라보았다.
 16|
 17|불과 몇 초 전만 하더라도 형형한 오라를 뿜어내던 그의 검은, 더욱 파괴적이고 예리한 무언가에 의해 반으로 잘려져 있었다.
 18|
 19|철컹.
 20|
 21|손아귀에서 미끄러진 검이 땅바닥을 나뒹군다. 한 박자 늦게 찾아온 고통이 송천우의 전신을 엄습했다.
 22|
 23|“쿨럭.”
 24|
 25|투두둑. 입가에서 쏟아진 검붉은 핏물이 눈 위를 적셨다. 옷과 갑옷이 비스듬히 갈라지고, 구릿빛의 상반신이 드러났다.
 26|
 27|그리고 탄탄한 근육과 피부 위를 가로지른 미세한 선이 붉게 달아오른 순간.
 28|
 29|촤아아악!
 30|
 31|엄청난 양의 핏물이 폭포수처럼 터져 나왔다.
 32|
 33|왼쪽 가슴으로부터 오른쪽 골반에 이르기까지. 벼락이 훑고 지나간 상흔(傷痕)은 극심했고 두 번 다시 아물지 않을 것이다.
 34|
 35|송천우는 힘이 풀리는 것을 느끼며 뒷걸음질 쳤다.
 36|
 37|사박.
 38|
 39|힘없는 발걸음이 피에 젖은 눈을 밟았다.
 40|
 41|한 걸음. 두 걸음. 세 걸음. 그리고…….
 42|
 43|푸스슥.
 44|
 45|쌓여 있던 눈이 떨어지는 소리에, 송천우는 간신히 신형을 바로잡았다.
 46|
 47|어느덧 그의 등 뒤에는 크레바스라 불리는 거대한 균열이 아가리를 쩍 벌린 채 기다리고 있었다.
 48|
 49|더 이상 물러설 곳도, 나아갈 곳도 없다.
 50|
 51|‘빌어먹을 일이로군.’
 52|
 53|송천우는 가슴이 공허해지는 것을 느꼈다.
 54|
 55|어쩌면 그것은 지금 이 순간조차도 자신의 몸에서 빠져나가는 생기(生氣) 때문일지도 모른다.
 56|
 57|문득 고개를 든 그의 시야에, 천천히 걸어오는 한 사람의 모습이 들어왔다.
 58|
 59|‘최민우.’
 60|
 61|언제나 존경과 두려움의 대상이었던 ‘그분’의 유일한 핏줄. 송천우는 벼락을 마주하기 직전 들었던 나직한 목소리를 떠올렸다.
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|‘내 몸 안에 흐르는 피가, 누구의 것인지 잊었습니까.’
 66|
 67|
 68|
 69|지금 이 순간, 노인의 눈동자에 비친 것은 이 자리에 없는 또 다른 누군가였다.
 70|
 71|이제는 과거의 기억으로만 남게 된 한 사람.
 72|
 73|그저 옆에서 지켜보는 것만으로도 존경과 두려움을 느낄 수밖에 없던 존재.
 74|
 75|송천우는 오랫동안 잊고 있던 사실을 깨달았다. 저 청년의 몸속에는, 천태민의 피가 흐르고 있다는 것을.
 76|
 77|“……형님?”
 78|
 79|송천우는 숨을 헐떡이며 중얼거렸다.
 80|
 81|온통 붉게 물든 시야 속, 찬란한 빛을 내뿜고 있는 검을 든 청년의 모습은 그의 외조부와 닮아 있었다.
 82|
 83|깊게 가라앉은 눈빛이 왜 변심했느냐 묻는 듯했다.
 84|
 85|“오지 마. 오지 마라!”
 86|
 87|송천우는 간신히 쥐어짠 외침과 함께 검을 휘둘렀다. 아니, 휘둘렀다고 생각했다.
 88|
 89|그러나 앞서 검을 떨어트린 그의 손은 텅 비어 있었고, 허공만을 휘젓던 손은 마침내 다가온 누군가의 단단한 손아귀에 가로막혔다.
 90|
 91|후우웅, 턱.
 92|
 93|송천우의 손목을 움켜쥔 최민우는 손아귀에 힘을 가했다. 으득, 뼈가 어긋나는 소리와 함께 비명이 터져 나왔다.
 94|
 95|“크아아아악!”
 96|
 97|털썩. 고통을 견디지 못하고 무릎을 꿇은 송천우를, 최민우는 가라앉은 눈빛으로 응시했다.
 98|
 99|지금 그의 눈에 비친 것은 송천우가 아니라 나이 든 노인이었다.
100|
101|츠츠츠츠.
102|
103|[영웅의 혼]에 서린 광휘가 서서히 사그라들었다. 이 싸움의 승부는 이미 결정되었다.
104|
105|쓰러진 패자를 향해, 우뚝 선 승자는 나직한 목소리로 이 치열한 싸움의 결과를 알려 주었다.
106|
107|“그만하십시오, 끝났습니다.”
108|
109|“……!”
110|
111|고통으로 몸부림치던 송천우의 신형이 우뚝 굳었다.
112|
113|자신이 패배하다니. 말도 안 되는 소리다. 그건 있을 수도 없고 있어서도 안 되는 일이었다.
114|
115|하지만 비로소 깨닫게 된 현실은 그렇지 않았다.
116|
117|파르르 떨리던 시선이 위를 향했다. 조금 전까지만 해도 벌어진 혈투가 무색할 만큼, 침착한 표정을 짓고 있는 최민우를 바라본 송천우가 중얼거렸다.
118|
119|“네가, 네가 어떻게?”
120|
121|“글쎄요.”
122|
123|최민우는 자신의 몸 안에 흐르는 막강한 기운을 느꼈다.
124|
125|불과 몇 달 전까지만 하더라도 알아차릴 수 없던 그것은 외조부가 그에게 남긴 유일한 선물이었고, 진태경은 그 포장지를 뜯어 주인에게 돌려주었다.
126|
127|선물을 유용하게 활용하는 방법과 함께.
128|
129|“그건 아마도…… 내가 당신보다 강했기 때문일 겁니다.”
130|
131|뿐만이 아니다. 최민우는 스스로를 믿었고, 올곧은 마음으로 행했다.
132|
133|그리고 자격을 갖춘 주인에게, 어느 영웅의 혼이 서린 검은 더욱 큰 힘을 선물했다.
134|
135|최민우는 힘 있는 눈빛으로 송천우를 내려다보았다.
136|
137|“나는 승리했고, 당신은 졌습니다. 우리에게 남은 사실은 그뿐입니다.”
138|
139|“……!”
140|
141|잘게 떨리던 노인의 시선이 차츰 가라앉았다. 피에 젖은 입술 사이로 갈라진 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
142|
143|“그래, 네 말대로다. 이런 결과는 예상치 못했지만.”
144|
145|“그 부분만큼은 저와 같군요. 저 역시 정말 이런 상황이 오리라고는 생각지 못했으니까요.”
146|
147|분노. 적개심. 밑바닥까지 추락한 인간을 향한 미약한 동정.
148|
149|송천우를 향한 최민우의 감정은 다양했으나, 그중에서도 가장 앞선 것은 의문이었다.
150|
151|도대체 왜. 무슨 이유로 송천우가 이런 짓을 벌였는지에 대한 의문. 그리고 앞서 그에게 들은 이야기에 대한 불신.
152|
153|“왜 이런 짓을 벌였습니까. 우리가 힘을 합쳤다면, 석고준을 몰아내고 아레스 길드를 장악하는 건 그리 어려운 일이 아니었을 겁니다.”
154|
155|최민우의 물음에, 송천우가 공허한 목소리로 대답했다.
156|
157|“안다. 나 역시 그렇게 생각했다.”
158|
159|“그렇다면 어째서?”
160|
161|“어쩔 수 없었다. 거절할 수 없는 제안이었어.”
162|
163|그리고 송천우에게 거절할 수 없는 제안을 건넨 사람의 이름을, 최민우는 이미 알고 있었다.
164|
165|“석고준. 모든 것이 그자의 명령이었습니까? 나와의 연합부터 지금까지, 모두 다?”
166|
167|“쿨럭. 명령?”
168|
169|다시 한번 핏물을 쏟아 낸 송천우가 힘없이 웃었다. 그건 석고준을 향한 명백한 조소(嘲笑)였다.
170|
171|“이정룡이라면 모를까. 그놈은 힘센 철부지에 불과하다. 내가 비록 비열하고 한심한 늙은이라고 해도, 그런 어린놈의 명령에 굴복할 정도는 아니야. 너와의 연합은 순전히 내 의지였다.”
172|
173|“그렇다면.”
174|
175|“말하지 않았느냐. 거절할 수 없는 제안이었다고.”
176|
177|금방이라도 꺼질 듯한 송천우의 눈동자를 들여다보던 최민우는 문득 깨달았다.
178|
179|눈앞의 노인에게 남은 것이 무엇인지. 거절할 수 없는 제안에 무엇이 들어가 있는지.
180|
181|“가족이군요.”
182|
183|작게 고개를 끄덕인 송천우가 입을 열었다.
184|
185|“이정룡과의 싸움에서 진 후에야 알았다. 가장 소중한 것을 잊고 있었다는 사실을.”
186|
187|치열했던 삶이었다.
188|
189|대격변 이전에는 가장으로서 밤낮없이 생계를 책임져야 했고, 대격변 중에는 전장을 떠날 수 없었으며, 대격변 이후에는 권력의 중심에 다가서기 위해 또 다른 싸움을 시작했으니까.
190|
191|그리고 이정룡과의 정쟁(政爭)에서 패하며 다시금 기억해 낸 가족의 소중함은, 이정룡의 죽음과 함께 깨어난 야심으로 잊혀졌다.
192|
193|“자리를 비운 것이 화근이었다. 늙은이가 뒤늦게 욕심을 부린 대가겠지.”
194|
195|“아마도 그 생각이 맞을 겁니다.”
196|
197|송천우의 한탄에 대답하는 최민우의 목소리는 냉정했다. 그의 말을 듣고 있자니 마지막 남아 있던 동정심마저 사라지는 기분이었다.
198|
199|“당신과 이정룡 때문에, 난 하나뿐인 가족을 잃어야 했습니다.”
200|
201|차가운 말투에는 불길이 담겨 있었다.
202|
203|두 어른의 야심에 의해, 야심이라는 단어의 뜻조차도 모르던 어린아이는 고아와 같은 신세가 됐다.
204|
205|부모의 죽음을 제대로 인지하기도 전에 사라진 외조부를 원망하며 지금껏 살아 와야 했다.
206|
207|“……미안하구나. 내 잘못이다.”
208|
209|“그럼 당장 태워 죽여도 할 말이 없겠군. 그렇지 않나?”
210|
211|허공에서 불쑥 들려온 목소리는 최민우가 아닌 다른 사람의 것이었다.
212|
213|사박. 예티의 푸른 피를 전신에 뒤집어쓴 김화종이 지면에 발을 내디뎠다.
214|
215|노 집사의 눈동자에는 손에 들린 불의 채찍과 같은 화염이 서려 있었다.
216|
217|“화종이. 자네였나.”
218|
219|“아가리 닥쳐라. 이 개새끼야. 네놈 때문에 도련님께서 얼마나-”
220|
221|당장이라도 채찍을 휘두르려는 김화종을 만류한 것은 최민우였다.
222|
223|가벼운 눈짓에 입을 꾹 다문 노복이 물러나자, 최민우의 시선이 송천우를 향했다.
224|
225|“그럼 외할아버님에 관한 이야기도 모두 거짓입니까?”
226|
227|“차라리 거짓이었다면 좋겠구나. 하지만 전부 사실이다. 이미 너무 멀리 와 버렸어.”
228|
229|대답의 의미를 알아듣지 못해 미간을 찌푸리는 김화종과 달리, 최민우는 내심 안도와 실망이 뒤섞인 한숨을 내쉬었다.
230|
231|외조부가 살아 있다는 사실은 기쁜 일이지만, 이십 년이 넘도록 의식을 잃은 상태라는 것이 마음에 걸렸다.
232|
233|하지만 그것은 나중의 일. 지금 당장은 송천우의 처분이 우선이었다.
234|
235|- 도련님.
236|
237|자신을 향한 대견함과 송천우에 대한 분노, 그리고 일말의 기대감이 섞여 있는 김화종의 메시지 마법에 최민우는 고개를 저었다.
238|
239|그가 무슨 말을 할지는 이미 알고 있었다.
240|
241|- 김 집사님. 그건 안 됩니다.
242|
243|- 안 된다니. 그게 무슨 말씀이십니까.
244|
245|- 포션을 주십시오. 우선 죽지 않을 만큼만 치료해야겠습니다.
246|
247|- 하지만……!
248|
249|뭔가 외치려던 김화종은 침착한 최민우의 시선에 애써 마음을 억눌렀다.
250|
251|그도 알고 있었다. 송천우는 살아 있는 것만으로도 결정적인 증인이자 증거라는 것을.
252|
253|다만 부정하고 싶을 뿐이었다.
254|
255|“김 집사님.”
256|
257|“빌어먹을. 알겠습니다.”
258|
259|중급 포션을 건네주며 욕설을 내뱉는 김화종의 모습에 최민우가 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
260|
261|“지금 제 앞에서 욕하신 겁니까?”
262|
263|“예, 했습니다. 왜요?”
264|
265|“이야기는 얼핏 들었지만, 제가 기억하는 모습과는 너무 다른데요.”
266|
267|“이게 접니다. 도련님 어릴 때만 해도 보고 배울까 싶어서 행동 조심, 입조심 했던 거죠.”
268|
269|“계속 조심하시지 왜…….”
270|
271|“도련님도 이제 곧 서른입니다. 기왕 이렇게 된 거, 보고 배우려면 배우십시오. 아니면 마시고.”
272|
273|어릴 적부터 곁을 지키던 그 사람이 맞나.
274|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

His chest felt hollow. Perhaps that was the life still draining out of him.

[P25]
Song raised his head. Someone was walking slowly toward him.

[P26]
*Choi Minwoo.*

[P27]
The only blood descendant of *that person*, whom Song had always respected and feared. He remembered the quiet words he had heard just before the lightning struck.

[P28]
*“Have you forgotten whose blood flows through my veins?”*

[P29]
But now Song saw someone else in the young man before him. Someone who existed only in his memories. Someone he could not have watched from nearby without feeling both reverence and fear.

[P30]
Song realized something he had long forgotten: Cheon Taemin’s blood flowed through Choi Minwoo’s veins.

[P31]
“…Hyung?”

[P32]
The word escaped between ragged breaths.

[P33]
Through Song’s blood-red vision, the young man holding a brilliantly shining sword looked like his maternal grandfather. His somber eyes seemed to ask why Song had changed sides.

[P34]
“Don’t come closer. Stay away!”

[P35]
Song shouted with what little strength he had left and swung his sword. Or thought he did.

[P36]
The hand that had dropped it moments earlier was empty. It swept through the air until someone’s firm grip stopped it.

[P37]
*Whooom. Thud.*

[P38]
Choi Minwoo seized Song’s wrist and squeezed.

[P39]
*Crunch.*

[P40]
Bones shifted out of place, and Song screamed.

[P41]
“GRAAAAAH!”

[P42]
*Thud.*

[P43]
Unable to bear the pain, Song fell to his knees. Choi gazed down at him, his eyes steady. What he saw now was not Song Cheonwoo, but an old man.

[P44]
*Zzt, zzt, zzt.*

[P45]
The radiance surrounding *Hero’s Soul* slowly faded. The fight had already been decided.

[P46]
“Stop. It’s over,” Choi said quietly.

[P47]
“…!”

[P48]
Song went rigid. He had lost? Impossible. It could not happen. It should not happen.

[P49]
But there was no denying it.

[P50]
His trembling gaze lifted to Choi, whose calm expression made the bloody fight they had just fought seem unreal.

[P51]
“How? How did you…?”

[P52]
“I’m not sure.”

[P53]
Choi felt the immense power flowing through his body. Only a few months ago, he had been unable to sense it. It was the only gift his maternal grandfather had left him, and Jin Taekyung had torn off the wrapping and given the gift to its owner—along with a lesson in how to use it.

[P54]
“Perhaps… because I was stronger than you.”

[P55]
That was not all. Choi had believed in himself and acted with an upright heart. In return, the sword imbued with a hero’s soul had granted its worthy wielder even greater strength.

[P56]
He looked down at Song, his gaze unwavering.

[P57]
“I won, and you lost. That’s all that matters now.”

[P58]
“…!”

[P59]
The old man’s trembling gaze gradually settled. A hoarse voice came through his bloodstained lips.

[P60]
“Yes. You’re right. Though I didn’t expect this outcome.”

[P61]
“Neither did I. I never thought we’d end up here.”

[P62]
Anger. Hostility. A faint trace of pity for a man who had fallen so far. Choi felt all of them, but above all, he wanted to know why.

[P63]
Why had Song done this? And could Choi believe what Song had told him earlier?

[P64]
“Why did you do it? If we’d worked together, driving Go Jun out and taking control of Ares Guild wouldn’t have been difficult.”

[P65]
“I know,” Song answered hollowly. “I thought so too.”

[P66]
“Then why?”

[P67]
“I had no choice. It was an offer I couldn’t refuse.”

[P68]
Choi already knew who had made that offer.

[P69]
“Go Jun. Was it all on his orders? Our alliance, everything up to now?”

[P70]
“Cough. Orders?”

[P71]
Song spat out more blood and gave a feeble laugh. He was plainly laughing at Go Jun.

[P72]
“If it had been Lee Jungryong, perhaps. But that bastard is just an overpowered, immature brat. I may be a despicable, pathetic old man, but I haven’t sunk so low that I’d obey a youngster like him. Forming an alliance with you was my own decision.”

[P73]
“Then—”

[P74]
“I told you. It was an offer I couldn’t refuse.”

[P75]
Choi looked into Song’s fading eyes and suddenly understood what the old man still had left—and what the offer must have involved.

[P76]
“Your family.”

[P77]
Song gave a small nod.

[P78]
“I didn’t realize until after I lost to Lee Jungryong. I’d forgotten what mattered most.”

[P79]
His had been a hard-fought life. Before the Great Cataclysm, he had worked day and night to support his family. During it, he had been unable to leave the battlefield. Afterward, he had begun another struggle to reach the center of power.

[P80]
Losing that political struggle to Lee Jungryong had reminded him how precious his family was. Then Lee’s death had rekindled his ambition, and Song had forgotten them again.

[P81]
“Leaving them alone was my mistake. I suppose this is the price of an old man getting greedy so late in life.”

[P82]
“You’re probably right.”

[P83]
Choi’s answer was cold. Hearing Song lament his own choices stripped away the last of his pity.

[P84]
“Because of you and Lee Jungryong, I lost the only family I had.”

[P85]
His voice was cold, but fury burned beneath it.

[P86]
Because of two adults’ ambitions, a child too young to know what ambition meant had been left little better than an orphan. Before he could even understand that his parents were dead, his maternal grandfather had disappeared too. Choi had lived all these years resenting him.

[P87]
“…I’m sorry. It was my fault.”

[P88]
“Then you have no objection if I burn you to death right now. Do you?”

[P89]
The voice came from somewhere above them. It was not Choi’s.

[P90]
*Crunch.*

[P91]
Kim Hwajong landed on the snow, covered head to toe in blue yeti blood. His eyes burned as fiercely as the whip of fire in his hand.

[P92]
“Hwa-jong. It’s you.”

[P93]
“Shut your fucking mouth, you bastard. Do you know how much the Young Master—”

[P94]
Kim looked ready to swing the whip, but a slight glance from Choi stopped him. The old butler pressed his lips together and stepped back.

[P95]
Choi turned to Song.

[P96]
“Then was everything you said about my grandfather a lie too?”

[P97]
“I wish it were. But it was all true. Things have already gone too far.”

[P98]
Kim frowned, unable to understand what Song meant. Choi let out a breath, torn between relief and disappointment.

[P99]
His grandfather was alive. That was welcome news, even if he had been unconscious for more than twenty years.

[P100]
But that could wait. For now, Choi had to decide what to do with Song.

[P101]
*—Young Master.*

[P102]
Kim’s message spell carried pride in Choi, fury toward Song, and a faint hope. Choi shook his head. He knew what the old butler wanted to say.

[P103]
*—Butler Kim. We can’t.*

[P104]
*—What do you mean, we can’t?*

[P105]
*—Give me a potion. We need to treat him just enough to keep him alive.*

[P106]
*—But…!*

[P107]
Kim looked ready to protest, but Choi’s calm gaze made him hold back. He knew Song was a crucial witness—and, while alive, evidence in his own right.

[P108]
He simply wished it weren’t so.

[P109]
“Butler Kim.”

[P110]
“Damn it. All right.”

[P111]
Kim cursed as he handed over a mid-grade potion. Choi’s eyes widened.

[P112]
“Did you just swear in front of me?”

[P113]
“Yes, I did. Why?”

[P114]
“I’d heard a little about this, but you’re nothing like the man I remember.”

[P115]
“This is who I am. When you were little, I watched what I did and said in case you picked it up from me.”

[P116]
“Why stop now…?”

[P117]
“You’re almost thirty. At this point, learn from me if you want. Or don’t.”

[P118]
*Is this really the man who’s been by my side since I was a child?*

[P119]
Choi let out a quiet laugh at the old butler’s gruff tone.

[P120]
“Butler Kim.”

[P121]
“What? And stop laughing. That’s no way to treat an elder.”

[P122]
“Thank you. For becoming my only family.”

[P123]
“…!”

[P124]
“I’ve always wanted to tell you that.”

[P125]
After saying it, Choi could not bring himself to meet the old butler’s eyes. He turned away without another word.

[P126]
Ahead of him, an old man lay half-buried in the snow, waiting for death.

[P127]
*Click.*

[P128]
Choi pulled the stopper from the potion. Its delicate, fresh scent drove back the smell of blood.

[P129]
Song watched him approach through eyes that seemed about to close for good.

[P130]
“Are you… going to save me?”

[P131]
“Do you want to live?”

[P132]
“I… That’s…”

[P133]
Choi felt a surge of disgust at his hesitation.

[P134]
“I want to kill you. A hundred times. A thousand.”

[P135]
“B-but my family…”

[P136]
“There must be a way to help them. We’ll deal with it once we’re out of here.”

[P137]
“…”

[P138]
“Choose.”

[P139]
Song hesitated, then nodded with a look of resignation.

[P140]
Choi gazed at him coldly and slowly tipped the potion.

[P141]
*Hiss.*

[P142]
The milky liquid touched Song’s wound, and it began to close, little by little. The healing was slight. But for someone else, even that much could be a lifeline—enough to muster one final burst of strength.

[P143]
*Thump!*

[P144]
Where had Song found it?

[P145]
Snow flew in every direction as he hurled himself backward with superhuman force and slipped into the vast crevasse.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
